newsitem.title: UK: UK's Friends Provident details 1996 bonus rates.
newsitem.headline: UK's Friends Provident details 1996 bonus rates.

text.p: UK mutual life insurer Friends Provident said on Monday the bonus rate for its ordinary conventional life policies for 1996 was 3.0 percent on the sum assured and 4.5 percent on accumulated bonuses.

This maintained rates for the previous year. But the final bonus rate for a 10-year policy was 7.5 percent, down from 10 percent for 1995, while the rate for a 40-year policy was 100 percent, up from 97.5 percent, the group said in a statement.

"With-profit policies continue to provide competitive long-term returns and represent one of the most attractive investment options for regular savers," Michael Doerr, Friends Provident's chief executive said.
The group said the regular bonus rate for its conventional individual self-employed and personal pension policies was unchanged at 4.0 percent and 5.0 percent on accumulated bonuses.

It said it had secured "competitive returns for investors over the medium to longer term" and following the declaration, "maturing Main Fund with-profit policyholders in 1997 will benefit from investment returns of 9.5 percent per annum and 13.2 percent per annum over 10 and 25 years respectively".
Friends Provident said these returns "compare favourably with an average inflation rate of 4.5 percent per annum and 8.3 percent respectively over 10 and 25 years".
